item.title: Nga Kor Ming Tells Rain Rave Critics to 'Stay Home' — A Knife Incident, 80,000 Crowd, and Zero Accountability Later
item.description:
Said by: Nga Kor Ming, Housing and Local Government Minister (DAP)

Category: Social

Date: 2026-05-03

📌 What Happened

On May 3, 2026, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming defended the government-backed Rain Rave Water Music Festival in Bukit Bintang, which drew 80,000 participants and 200,000 online viewers. Echoing Tourism Minister Tiong King Sing, Nga told critics: “For those who disagree, it is your right to choose to stay at home and not to come. Simple as that.” He framed the event as proof that “Malaysia Truly Asia is not a slogan but our culture and way of life.” His statement came the same day the South China Morning Post reported that a 28-year-old woman carrying a knife had been tackled and arrested by the crowd at the festival on Saturday night.

item.title: [BM] Tiong King Sing Suruh Pengkritik 'Berhenti Mempolitikkan' Pesta Air Anjuran Kerajaan — Selepas Kementeriannya Sendiri Dicela PM Atas Isu Arak
item.description:
Said by: Tiong King Sing, Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister

Category: Social

Date: 2026-05-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Pada 1 Mei 2026, Menteri Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing menolak kritikan yang semakin meningkat terhadap Rain Rave Water Music Festival 2026, yang diadakan malam sebelumnya di Bukit Bintang di bawah kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026. Tiong menyuruh pengkritik “berhenti mempolitikkan” acara itu, mendakwa lebih 50,000 orang hadir, berbangga kerana basah di atas pentas, dan menegaskan pesta itu “bukan Songkran” — sambil menunjukkan apa yang beliau panggil “piawai berganda” kerana perayaan Songkran di Kedah pada 18 April tidak menghadapi tentangan serupa. Beliau mengesahkan telah menerima memorandum daripada pengkritik yang menuntut peletakan jawatannya.

item.title: Fahmi's MCMC Escalates Digital Crackdown — Grindr and Blued Purged From App Stores as Government Replaces 'LGBT' With 'Deviant Culture'
item.description:

Category: Social

Date: 2026-03-12

📌 What Happened

Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil confirmed on February 25, in a written parliamentary reply, that the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had blocked access to LGBTQ dating websites Grindr and Blued, and was “studying legal measures” to curb their mobile apps. By early March, both platforms were removed from Google Play and the Apple App Store in Malaysia — an escalation from website blocking to full digital erasure. Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced a proposed Cyber Crime Bill that would expand the government’s legal powers to restrict such platforms.
